name: Go (Golang)
statement: No production Go experience. What transfers is a track record of getting productive fast in unfamiliar, complicated systems — expect to be reviewing pull requests within a couple of weeks rather than a couple of months, given the syntax-level size of the gap coming from other statically-typed languages.

name: Rust
statement: No production Rust experience. Unlike a syntax-level gap, Rust's ownership and borrowing model is a genuinely new runtime model, so this would be a ramp measured in months rather than weeks.

name: Java
statement: No production Java experience. Backend patterns from typed, convention-driven frameworks used elsewhere carry over conceptually; the gap is syntax and ecosystem, not architecture.

name: .NET
statement: No production .NET/C# experience. Closest overlap is backend work in NestJS and other typed, convention-driven server frameworks.

name: GraphQL
statement: No production GraphQL experience — API work to date has been REST throughout. Expect a syntax-level ramp on schemas and resolvers on top of existing API-design experience, not a conceptual one.

name: Native Mobile (iOS/Android)
statement: No native iOS/Android development (Swift, Kotlin or Objective-C). Past mobile work was delivered through hybrid, web-based frameworks rather than native platform APIs.

name: Django
statement: No production Django experience. Backend framework depth is concentrated in NestJS and other convention-driven frameworks; Python itself is real production experience (the open-source cowork CLI is a Python codebase), but framework-level Django depth specifically has not been exercised on the job.

name: Shopify
statement: No production Shopify experience, including platform-specific surfaces such as Checkout Extensibility or the GraphQL Admin API.
